newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls Christopher meeting important.
newsitem.headline: China calls Christopher meeting important.

text.p: China said on Tuesday a planned visit by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher was important to Sino-U.S. ties and that the two sides would find they had more interests in common than differences.
"This is an important bilateral meeting," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told reporters, referring to the visit later this month.
The spokesman sidestepped a question whether a dispute over textiles would be part of discussions during the visit, saying only that details had not been worked out.
But he said there was no reason for China and the United States not to develop a healthy and stable relationship.
"We will discover that in general, the common interests of China and the United States are far greater than the differences," Cui said.

China and the United States have both said they saw an improvement in ties strained by disputes over Taiwan, human rights, arms proliferation and trade over the past year. Beijing said on Sunday it would suspend imports of some U.S. goods in retaliation for U.S. penalties on Chinese textiles.
